title: Krakatoa 1883 air wave: passage times I-VII at 47 barographs (Strachey 1888)
verdict_rule: Laps that change with the station's position, as any echo would make them, or no regular passages after the first two.

sources.cite: G. J. Symons (ed.), The Eruption of Krakatoa and Subsequent Phenomena, Report of the Krakatoa Committee of the Royal Society (London: Trübner, 1888), Part II: R. Strachey, "On the air waves and sounds caused by the eruption of Krakatoa in August, 1883", pp. 57-88; Tables II-IV (pp. 62, 65-67) and VIII (pp. 75-76)

units.t: hours after 0 h GMT, 27 August 1883 (h:mm in the CSV)
units.lat: degrees, N positive (deg min hemisphere in the CSV)
units.lon: degrees, E positive (deg min hemisphere in the CSV)
units.flags: ? queried by Strachey; * time from Prof. Ragona (Modena); + Palermo

inputs.origin: R. Strachey in Symons (ed.), The Eruption of Krakatoa (Royal Society, 1888), Part II, tables III, IV and VIII, Internet Archive scan.
inputs.checks: The build checks the 175 intervals of table VIII against the transcribed times.
inputs.caveats: Strachey's velocities and degrees are not taken (they used the radius of his day).
